# Pet Insurance Decisions - full fact list

> What pet insurance covers, what it costs, and what the fine print says - every fact read from the brand's own official page, with its source and check date.

Every entry below was read from the official page named in its source URL and checked on the date shown. Figures are quoted as published; conditions are stated because the number usually depends on them.

## Lemonade pet insurance

URL: https://furadvisor.com/lemonade-pet-insurance

- **Starts at $10/mo** - Basic accident and illness coverage; actual price varies by coverage choices, breed, age and location (Lemonade cost guide, last updated Jun 3, 2026).
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)

### Facts

- Waiting periods: 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions; benefits of the preventative package can be used the day after the policy is purchased. (condition: As described in the FAQ on Lemonade's pet insurance page.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Pre-existing conditions are not covered; accidents and new illnesses are covered as part of base coverage once waiting periods are up. (condition: Anything the pet showed signs of before the waiting periods are up counts as pre-existing.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Covered items listed on the official page include bloodwork, X-rays, MRI, CT scans, lab work, ultrasounds, cancer, emergency care, surgery, heart disease, hospitalization, road accidents, outpatient care, allergy medicine, specialty care, injections, prescription medications, arthritis medication, and knee/elbow/hip dysplasia. (condition: Listed under the coverage section of Lemonade's pet insurance page; coverage remains subject to policy terms.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Any vet in the United States can be used, as long as they are licensed to provide vet care in their state. (condition: Stated on the pet insurance page; no vet network restriction is described.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- You can cancel at any time in the Lemonade app; you get a refund if it is within the first 30 days, and waiting periods reset after cancellation. (condition: Refund window is the first 30 days of the policy.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Vet exam fees are only covered if you buy the Visit Fee Add-on, and only when the visit is for treating a covered accident or illness. (condition: Add-on must be purchased; the add-on does not cover routine wellness visits.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Policies for dogs and cats start at $10/month. (condition: Basic accident and illness coverage; the cost guide states cost varies by coverage amount/type, breed, age and where you live.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade pet parents pay around $48/month for dogs and around $27/month for cats on average. (condition: Stated as on-average figures across different ages, breeds and locations on the cost guide page (last updated Jun 3, 2026).)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Example quote: a 4-year-old Goldendoodle in Chicago with 80% co-insurance, the maximum annual limit available and a $250 deductible was quoted at $61/month. (condition: Lemonade's own example quote for that specific pet profile, shown in its comparison table.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Example quote: a 1-year-old short-haired cat in Danbury, Connecticut with a $250 deductible, 80% co-insurance and the maximum annual limit was quoted at $29/month. (condition: Lemonade's own example quote for that specific pet profile, base policy with no add-ons or discounts applied.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Deductible options are $100, $250, $500, $750, or $1,000. (condition: Listed on the cost guide as choices that lower the premium.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Discounts published on the official site: multi-pet discount, bundle discount with other Lemonade policies, and a discount for paying annually instead of monthly. (condition: Listed among premium-lowering options on the cost guide; eligibility varies.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Multi-pet discount eligibility depends on where you live. (condition: Stated in the coverage guide FAQ; the discount is removed from your remaining policy if you cancel all but one pet policy.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Preventative add-on packages: Preventative for Adult Pets from +$10/Mo, Preventative+ for Adult Pets from +$15/Mo, Preventative for Puppies/Kittens from +$31/Mo. (condition: 'From' prices as published; package availability depends on your location.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- A quote can be completed in as little as 90 seconds. (condition: Stated on the cost guide page.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade reports 4.9 stars in the App Store and on Google Play. (condition: Self-reported rating displayed on Lemonade's pet insurance page.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Each pet needs its own policy. (condition: Stated in the pet insurance page FAQ; pets are set up one at a time.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- No dedicated promo code or coupon page appears in Lemonade's official sitemap. (condition: Sitemap at https://www.lemonade.com/sitemap.xml checked on 2026-09-25; no URL matching promo, coupon, discount or deal was found. The published discounts are the multi-pet, bundle and annual-payment discounts listed above.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **How much does Lemonade pet insurance cost?** Lemonade states that policies for dogs and cats start at $10/month for basic accident and illness coverage. Its own averages are around $48/month for dogs and around $27/month for cats; its example quotes are $61/month for a 4-year-old Goldendoodle in Chicago and $29/month for a 1-year-old short-haired cat in Danbury, Connecticut, both at $250 deductible and 80% co-insurance. Cost varies by coverage, breed, age and location.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How do I get a Lemonade pet insurance quote?** Lemonade's own site says a quote takes as little as 90 seconds. The quote entry point on its pet insurance page is labeled 'CHECK OUR PRICES'.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What does Lemonade pet insurance cover?** The official page lists bloodwork, X-rays, MRI, CT scans, lab work, ultrasounds, cancer, emergency care, surgery, heart disease, hospitalization, road accidents, outpatient care, allergy medicine, specialty care, injections, prescription medications, arthritis medication and knee/elbow/hip dysplasia. Vet exam fees are covered only with the Visit Fee Add-on and only for a covered accident or illness. Coverage is subject to policy terms.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What are Lemonade pet insurance waiting periods?** 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions. If you bought a preventative package, its benefits can be used the day after purchase.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Are there Lemonade pet insurance promo codes or discounts?** Lemonade's official sitemap contains no promo code or coupon page (checked 2026-09-25). The discounts published on its own site are a multi-pet discount (eligibility depends on where you live), a bundle discount with other Lemonade policies, and a discount for paying annually instead of monthly.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What do reviews of Lemonade pet insurance say on its own site?** Lemonade reports 4.9 stars in the App Store and on Google Play on its pet insurance page. That is Lemonade's self-reported figure, not an independent audit.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)

## Spot pet insurance

URL: https://furadvisor.com/spot-pet-insurance

- **Dogs from $15/mo, cats from $9/mo** - Advertised premiums: the dog figure is from an accident and illness plan with 80% reimbursement rate, $500 annual deductible and $2,500 annual limit for a 2-year-old small mixed dog (11-25 lbs) in ZIP 32009; the cat figure is from 80% reimbursement, $750 annual deductible and $2,500 annual limit for a 2-year-old mixed cat in ZIP 33801. Plan costs vary.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)

### Facts

- Spot reimburses up to 90% of covered vet bills. (condition: Reimbursement percentage is a plan choice; actual reimbursement depends on plan type and options including annual limit, co-insurance and deductible.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Dog insurance starts from $15/month and cat insurance starts from $9/month. (condition: Advertised premium for the dog figure: accident and illness plan, 80% reimbursement rate, $500 annual deductible, $2,500 annual limit, 2-year-old small mixed dog (11-25 lbs) in ZIP 32009. Cat figure: 80% reimbursement, $750 annual deductible, $2,500 annual limit, 2-year-old mixed cat in ZIP 33801. Plan costs vary; premiums may increase or decrease with pet age.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- 10% multi-pet discount for every pet enrolled after the first. (condition: Discounts vary by state and are subject to change; more information is shown at checkout.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/cat-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Claims are reimbursed in 48 hours or less, and most claims are processed in under 2 business days. (condition: '48 hrs or less' is based on Spot admin data from 2019 to 2024; 'under 2 business days' is stated in the site FAQ. Actual reimbursement amounts vary by plan and claim.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Sample claim shown on the official page: total vet bill $12,345, Spot plan reimbursed $11,110. (condition: Based on actual policyholder claims from 2023; the example uses an accident and illness policy at $75.01/month with a $500 deductible, 90% reimbursement and unlimited annual benefit for a 1-year-old giant mix dog. Individual reimbursement amounts may vary.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- 30-day money-back guarantee. (condition: Applies to cancellations made within 30 days of the policy's start date if no claims have been filed and no covered expenses were applied to the deductible or reimbursed. Not available in NY; 15-day guarantee in ME, LA and WA. Cancellations must be requested via email, phone or written notice.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot plans typically have a 14-day waiting period for coverage. (condition: Read from the sample Accident & Illness policy PDF linked on spotpet.com/sample-policy (California form PET-P-20000-CA-IAIC-1024): 14 days for illness including congenital, hereditary and orthopedic illness, beginning on the first effective date of coverage. A paid Waiting Period Health Assessment can modify it; state forms differ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-25)
- Pre-existing conditions are not covered; a curable condition that has been symptom-free and treatment-free for 180 days is no longer considered pre-existing and can become eligible. (condition: The 180-day symptom- and treatment-free rule is stated in the site FAQ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Puppies and kittens 8 weeks and older can be covered; there is no upper age limit, no lifetime cap, and no vet exam is needed for enrollment. (condition: Stated on the official page comparison section and FAQ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Coverage includes dental illnesses, breed-specific/chronic/hereditary conditions, prescription foods, a 24/7 pet health helpline, behavioral modification and microchip implantation. (condition: Dental illness and hereditary condition coverage only apply with an accident and illness plan. Prescription food and supplements are covered only when prescribed to treat an eligible accident or illness, not for weight management or general health maintenance. Pre-existing conditions are not covered.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- The optional preventative care add-on has no deductible and no waiting period - benefits start the next day. (condition: Add-on costs extra; stated on the dog insurance page.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/dog-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot Perks gives access to $2,500+ in discounts on pet brands. (condition: No purchase necessary; based on total combined Spot Perks discounts applied to average vendor cart value; terms at spotpet.com/perks-terms.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- An employee discount advertised at 20% appears on Spot's plan pages for employer benefits. (condition: Footnote: includes up to 10% group discount plus up to 10% multi-pet discount on 2nd+ pets. Discounts vary by state, are subject to change, and are not available in all states.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/dog-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot plans are underwritten by Independence American Insurance Company (NAIC #26581) or United States Fire Insurance Company, and produced by Spot Pet Insurance Services, LLC (NPN #19246385). (condition: Underwriter disclosure in the page footer; which carrier applies depends on the policy.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot displays a rating of 4.7 / 5 based on 8,300+ reviews. (condition: Rating as displayed on Spot's homepage; it is the company's own displayed figure.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- You can visit any licensed vet in the United States or Canada. (condition: No network restrictions; stated on the homepage and FAQ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- No dedicated promo code page appears in Spot's official sitemaps. (condition: Sitemap index at https://spotpet.com/sitemap.xml and its child sitemaps checked on 2026-09-25; no URL matching promo or coupon was found. The published discounts are the multi-pet discount, the group/employee discount and Spot Perks.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **How much does Spot pet insurance cost?** Spot advertises dog insurance starting from $15/month and cat insurance starting from $9/month. The dog figure assumes an accident and illness plan with 80% reimbursement, a $500 annual deductible and a $2,500 annual limit for a 2-year-old small mixed dog in ZIP 32009; the cat figure assumes 80% reimbursement, a $750 deductible and a $2,500 annual limit for a 2-year-old mixed cat in ZIP 33801. Plan costs vary by coverage, breed, age and location.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How do I get a Spot pet insurance quote?** Spot's official page has a 'Click For Price' button that opens its quote flow at spotpet.com/quote. The site FAQ says to see your price you get a free quote, because cost depends on coverage, age, breed and location.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What does Spot pet insurance cover?** Accident-only and accident and illness plans are offered, plus an optional preventive care add-on. The accident and illness plan covers dental illnesses, hereditary and breed-specific conditions, prescription foods when prescribed for an eligible accident or illness, behavioral modification, microchip implantation and a 24/7 pet health helpline. Pre-existing conditions are not covered.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What are Spot pet insurance waiting periods?** Spot plans typically have a 14-day waiting period; state-specific waiting periods vary and are listed in the sample policy. The preventative care add-on has no waiting period - its benefits start the next day.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Are there Spot pet insurance promo codes or discounts?** Spot's official sitemaps contain no promo code page (checked 2026-09-25). Discounts published on its own site: 10% off for every pet enrolled after the first, an advertised 20% employee discount through employer benefits (up to 10% group discount plus up to 10% multi-pet discount on 2nd+ pets, varies by state, not available in all states), and Spot Perks with $2,500+ in brand discounts.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/cat-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What do reviews of Spot pet insurance say on its own site?** Spot displays 4.7 / 5 based on 8,300+ reviews on its homepage. That is the company's own displayed figure.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)

## Fetch pet insurance

URL: https://furadvisor.com/fetch-pet-insurance

- **Avg $35/mo dogs, $22/mo cats** - Based on U.S. annual premiums using the most common coverage configuration of a $10,000 annual limit, $300 deductible and 80% reimbursement rate for the period 07.01.2024 through 06.30.2025.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/pet-insurance-cost (checked 2026-09-25)

### Facts

- Average monthly price: $35/month for dogs and $22/month for cats. (condition: Based on U.S. annual premiums using the most common coverage configuration of a $10,000 annual limit, $300 deductible and 80% reimbursement rate for the period 07.01.2024 through 06.30.2025 (Fetch data).)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/pet-insurance-cost (checked 2026-09-25)
- Breed averages on the official price page: French Bulldog $71/mo, German Shepherd $53/mo, Golden Doodle $50/mo, Golden Retriever $50/mo, Maltipoo $35/mo, Shih-Tzu $30/mo for dogs; Siamese $29/mo, Maine Coon $35/mo, Mixed Breed $27/mo and Domestic Shorthair $24/mo for cats. (condition: Shown as 'on avg.' figures on Fetch's price page; the same average-premium footnote applies (period 07.01.2024-06.30.2025, $10,000 annual limit, $300 deductible, 80% reimbursement).)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/pet-insurance-cost (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch covers up to 90% of unexpected vet bills. (condition: Reimbursement percentage is part of the plan; payment follows claim approval and the deductible being met.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- The waiting period for accident and illness coverage with Fetch is up to 15 days. (condition: Fetch states it emails you as soon as your coverage starts.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch covers dogs and cats 6 weeks and older. (condition: Stated in the official FAQ; enrolling early avoids conditions later being classed as pre-existing.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Pre-existing conditions are not covered. (condition: A condition that occurred, or showed clinical signs, before enrollment, during the waiting period, or before the pet's first exam counts as pre-existing.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Sick-visit exam fees are covered: every sick visit comes with an exam fee of up to $250 and Fetch covers those. (condition: Stated on the official homepage coverage section.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Online vet visits are covered up to $1,000 per year, included at no extra cost with no copay. (condition: Members get 24/7 access to licensed veterinarians; stated in the official FAQ and coverage section.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- 100% reimbursement on hundreds of qualifying pet meds through Fetch Pet Rx. (condition: Subject to deductible and policy limit; applies to qualifying medications purchased from FetchPetRx.com (fulfilled by Allivet) or Allivet.com, as designated in the Terms & Conditions.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Claims are typically processed in less than 10 days. (condition: Stated in the official 'How Fetch works' section; payment follows approval and the deductible being met, by direct deposit.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Veterans and active military save 10% on their Fetch pet insurance policy every month for life. (condition: Discounts and offers are subject to approval and may change at any time; the maximum available discount is 10%, it may not be available in all states, and it is not valid with any other offer.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/military-pet-insurance-discount (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch publishes $1,500+ in members-only savings with its Health Perks, and its Fetch Deals page states members save an average of $40+ per order. (condition: $1,500+ shown in the Health Perks section of fetchpet.com; the $40+ average is stated twice on fetchpet.com/deals (Fetch member purchase data). Both are the brand's own figures.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Every adult tooth is covered - injury and disease in every adult tooth, not just the canines. (condition: Stated in the official homepage coverage section; all coverage is subject to policy limits.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Sample claim shown on the official price page: patella surgery cost $28,776, Fetch paid back $21,331. (condition: Claim example displayed on Fetch's price page; individual results vary by plan and claim.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/pet-insurance-cost (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch insurance policies are administered by Fetch Insurance Services, LLC and underwritten by AXIS Insurance Company in the U.S. and AXIS Reinsurance Company (Canadian Branch) in Canada. (condition: Underwriter disclosure in the homepage footer.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch states that any veterinarian in the U.S. or Canada can be used, including specialists and emergency clinics. (condition: No network restriction described in the official FAQ.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- No dedicated promo code page appears in Fetch's official sitemap. (condition: Sitemap at https://fetchpet.com/sitemap.xml checked on 2026-09-25; no URL matching promo or coupon was found. The published discounts are the 10% military discount (maximum available discount is 10% per the site footnote) and the Fetch Deals member savings.)
  Source: https://fetchpet.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **How much does Fetch pet insurance cost?** Fetch publishes averages of $35/month for dogs and $22/month for cats, based on U.S. annual premiums with the most common configuration of a $10,000 annual limit, $300 deductible and 80% reimbursement rate for 07.01.2024 through 06.30.2025. Its breed averages run from $24/month (Domestic Shorthair cats) to $71/month (French Bulldogs). Your price varies by pet age, breed and where you live.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/pet-insurance-cost (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How do I get a Fetch pet insurance quote?** Fetch's quote flow starts from the 'Get your price' button on its official site, which opens its pet setup page at fetchpet.com/mypet. Fetch states your quote includes all monthly taxes and fees.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What does Fetch pet insurance cover?** Accident and illness coverage with up to 90% reimbursement, exam fees up to $250 per sick visit, every adult tooth (not just canines), online vet visits up to $1,000 per year at no extra cost, and 100% reimbursement on qualifying pet meds through Fetch Pet Rx (subject to deductible and policy limit). A Wellness add-on covers routine and preventive care. Pre-existing conditions are not covered.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What are Fetch pet insurance waiting periods?** The waiting period for accident and illness coverage with Fetch is up to 15 days. Fetch emails you as soon as your coverage starts.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Are there Fetch pet insurance promo codes or discounts?** Fetch's official sitemap contains no promo code page (checked 2026-09-25). Discounts published on its own site: veterans and active military save 10% every month for life (maximum available discount is 10%, subject to approval, may not be available in all states, not valid with any other offer), and Fetch Deals member savings of $1,500+ included at no extra cost.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/military-pet-insurance-discount (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What do reviews of Fetch pet insurance say on its own site?** Fetch's homepage says thousands of 5-star reviews on Trustpilot and labels itself '#1 Pet Insurance, Readers' Choice 2026'. Those are the company's own claims as displayed on its site.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)

- Fetch covers sick-visit exam fees: every sick visit comes with an exam fee of up to $250 and Fetch covers those. (condition: Stated in the official homepage coverage section; coverage remains subject to policy terms.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch online vet visits are covered up to $1,000 per year, included at no extra cost with no copay. (condition: Members get 24/7 access to licensed veterinarians; stated in the official FAQ and coverage section.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch claims are typically processed in less than 10 days. (condition: Stated in the official 'How Fetch works' section; payment follows approval and the deductible being met, by direct deposit.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Veterans and active military save 10% on their Fetch pet insurance policy every month for life. (condition: Discounts and offers are subject to approval and may change at any time; the maximum available discount is 10%, it may not be available in all states, and it is not valid with any other offer.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/military-pet-insurance-discount (checked 2026-09-25)
- No dedicated promo code or coupon page appears in Lemonade's official sitemap. (condition: Sitemap checked on 2026-09-25; no URL matching promo, coupon, discount or deal was found. Published discounts are multi-pet, bundle and annual payment.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)
- No dedicated promo code page appears in Spot's official sitemap. (condition: Sitemap index and its child sitemaps checked on 2026-09-25; no URL matching promo or coupon was found. Published discounts are multi-pet, group/employee and Spot Perks.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)
- No dedicated promo code page appears in Fetch's official sitemap. (condition: Sitemap checked on 2026-09-25; no URL matching promo or coupon was found. Published discounts are the 10% military discount and Fetch Deals member savings.)
  Source: https://fetchpet.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **What is the best pet insurance in 2026?** There is no single best pet insurance - the honest answer depends on which published fact you care about. Lemonade publishes the lowest starting price (from $10/month), Spot publishes the fastest claim payment (48 hours or less, based on Spot admin data 2019-2024) and Fetch publishes the most detailed pricing (breed-by-breed averages with a stated methodology). Compare quotes for your own pet on each official site, because advertised prices are quoted under different deductible, limit and reimbursement conditions.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Which pet insurance is cheapest?** The lowest published starting prices are Lemonade at $10/month for dogs and cats, Spot at $15/month for dogs and $9/month for cats, and Fetch, which does not publish an entry price but publishes averages of $35/month for dogs and $22/month for cats. These figures are not directly comparable: Spot's price assumes an 80% reimbursement rate, a $500 deductible and a $2,500 annual limit for a specific dog in ZIP 32009, while Fetch's average assumes a $10,000 annual limit, a $300 deductible and 80% reimbursement. Your real price comes from a quote on the brand's official site.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Is there a real pet insurance promo code?** Not from these three brands. Their official sitemaps were checked on 2026-09-25 and none contains a promo code or coupon page. The discounts that do exist on the official sites are Lemonade's multi-pet, bundle and annual-payment discounts, Spot's 10% multi-pet discount and its group/employee discount, and Fetch's 10% military discount plus Fetch Deals member savings. Third-party coupon sites are not a source we use.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How long are pet insurance waiting periods?** Published waiting periods: Lemonade 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions (preventative package benefits start the day after purchase); Spot typically 14 days, with state-specific variations detailed in its sample policy; Fetch up to 15 days for accident and illness coverage. Coverage for anything that shows signs before those periods end counts as pre-existing.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Does pet insurance cover pre-existing conditions?** No. All three brands state that pre-existing conditions are not covered. Spot additionally publishes that a curable condition which has been symptom-free and treatment-free for 180 days is no longer considered pre-existing and can become eligible. Fetch counts anything that occurred or showed clinical signs before enrolment, during the waiting period, or before the pet's first exam as pre-existing.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Do I need a vet exam to buy pet insurance?** Spot states no vet exam is needed for enrolment and has no upper age limit, with puppies and kittens 8 weeks and older eligible. Fetch covers dogs and cats 6 weeks and older and advises enrolling early so conditions are not later classed as pre-existing. For Lemonade, an enrolment exam requirement is not published on the official pages checked on 2026-09-25.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)

- Lemonade policies for dogs and cats start at $10/month. (condition: Basic accident and illness coverage; the cost guide states cost varies by coverage amount and type, breed, age and where you live.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)

  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **How much does pet insurance cost per month?** The entry points the brands publish are $10/month for dogs and cats at Lemonade, $15/month for dogs and $9/month for cats at Spot, and averages of $35/month for dogs and $22/month for cats at Fetch. Lemonade's own averages across its policyholders are about $48/month for dogs and about $27/month for cats. Every one of those figures is tied to a stated deductible, annual limit and reimbursement rate, so the only number that describes your pet is the quote the brand's own site produces.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What makes one pet insurance quote more expensive than another?** Lemonade lists breed and age, location and state, the coverage options chosen (deductible amount, co-insurance percentage and annual limits), any add-ons, and available discounts. Spot adds that premiums are based on the current age of your pet and may increase at renewal, and that species or breed and home address can change the initial premium.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How can I lower my monthly premium?** Lemonade's cost guide suggests choosing a higher deductible ($100, $250, $500, $750 or $1,000), selecting a lower annual coverage limit, or skipping optional add-ons, and notes that adjusting these levels might lower the premium by 10% or 15% - at the price of being covered for less. Fetch publishes the same mechanic: a higher deductible makes the price lower, and a lower reimbursement rate makes the price lower.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Does location change what pet insurance costs?** On Lemonade's published state table, average monthly cost ranges from $30 to $34 in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Georgia and Michigan up to $45 to $49 in California and Connecticut. Those averages come from Lemonade's own policy rates as of October 2024 and the page calls them illustrative; Spot and Fetch do not publish a state table.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Which is cheaper, Lemonade or Spot?** On published entry prices Lemonade is lower for dogs ($10/month against Spot's $15/month) and Spot is lower for cats ($9/month against Lemonade's $10/month starting price). The comparison stops there, because Spot's figures assume an 80% reimbursement rate, a $500 or $750 deductible and a $2,500 annual limit for specific pets in specific ZIP codes, while Lemonade's figures assume basic accident and illness coverage. Both brands publish averages only in part: Lemonade publishes about $48/month for dogs and about $27/month for cats, and Spot publishes no average of its own.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What discounts can lower the price?** Lemonade publishes a multi-pet discount (eligibility depends on where you live), a bundle discount with other Lemonade policies, and a discount for paying annually instead of monthly. Spot publishes 10% off every pet enrolled after the first and an advertised 20% employee discount. Fetch publishes 10% off every month for life for veterans and active military. None of the three brands publishes a promo code page in its official sitemap.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Does pet insurance cost more as my pet gets older?** Spot states on its homepage that premiums are based on the current age of your pet and may increase due to the age of your pet at renewal, and that initial premiums can be affected by species or breed and by home address. Lemonade lists age among the factors that change the cost. The published starting prices on this page therefore describe young pets on the stated configurations, not every age.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)

## Lemonade vs Spot Pet Insurance: Which One Should You Pick?

URL: https://furadvisor.com/lemonade-vs-spot

Keyword: lemonade vs spot pet insurance

### Facts

- Lemonade policies for dogs and cats start at $10/month for basic accident and illness coverage. (condition: Cost varies by coverage amount and type, breed, age and where you live.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot advertises dog insurance from $15/month and cat insurance from $9/month. (condition: Dog figure assumes 80% reimbursement, $500 annual deductible and $2,500 annual limit for a 2-year-old small mixed dog (11-25 lbs) in ZIP 32009; cat figure assumes 80% reimbursement, $750 deductible and $2,500 limit for a 2-year-old mixed cat in ZIP 33801. Plan costs vary.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade publishes averages of about $48/month for dogs and about $27/month for cats across different ages, breeds and locations. (condition: Stated on the cost guide; Spot publishes no average of its own.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade waiting periods are 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions, and preventative package benefits can be used the day after purchase. (condition: As described in the FAQ on Lemonade's pet insurance page.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot's sample Accident & Illness policy states a 14-day waiting period for illness, including congenital anomaly or disorder, hereditary disorder and orthopedic illness, beginning on the first effective date of coverage. (condition: Read from the sample policy PDF linked on spotpet.com/sample-policy (California form PET-P-20000-CA-IAIC-1024); a paid Waiting Period Health Assessment can modify the waiting period and state forms differ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade states it pays 50% of eligible claims instantly through AI. (condition: Stated on the cost guide; the remainder follows review, and payment goes to the bank details entered in the app.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot states claims are reimbursed in 48 hours or less, with most claims processed in under 2 business days. (condition: '48 hrs or less' is based on Spot admin data from 2019 to 2024; actual reimbursement depends on plan type, annual limit, co-insurance, deductible and policy terms.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot's published sample claim reimbursed $11,110 of a $12,345 vet bill. (condition: 2023 policyholder claim on an accident and illness policy at $75.01/month with a $500 deductible, 90% reimbursement and unlimited annual benefit.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade does not cover pre-existing conditions; anything the pet showed signs of before the waiting periods are up counts as pre-existing. (condition: Accidents and new illnesses are covered as base coverage once waiting periods are up.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot does not cover pre-existing conditions, but a cured and curable condition symptom-free and treatment-free for 180 days stops being classed as pre-existing. (condition: The 180-day rule excludes knee and ligament injuries; stated in the site FAQ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade deductible options are $100, $250, $500, $750 or $1,000, and annual limits can be set between $5,000 and $100,000. (condition: Both listed on the cost guide as choices that change the premium.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot reimburses up to 90% of covered vet bills, and both advertised quotes use an 80% reimbursement rate with a $2,500 annual limit. (condition: Reimbursement and limits are plan choices; actual reimbursement depends on plan options and policy terms.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade allows any vet in the United States licensed to provide vet care in their state; Spot allows any licensed vet in the United States or Canada. (condition: No network restriction is described on either brand's own page.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot covers puppies and kittens 8 weeks and older, has no upper age limit and needs no vet exam to enrol. (condition: Stated in the official page comparison section and FAQ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot states that premiums are based on the current age of your pet and may increase due to the age of your pet at renewal. (condition: Footnote on Spot's plan pages; initial premiums may also be affected by species or breed and by home address.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade publishes three discounts: a multi-pet discount whose eligibility depends on where you live, a bundle discount with other Lemonade policies, and a discount for paying annually instead of monthly. (condition: Listed among premium-lowering options on the cost guide; eligibility and availability vary.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot publishes a 10% discount for every pet enrolled after the first, an advertised 20% employee discount, and Spot Perks with $2,500+ in discounts on pet brands. (condition: The employee discount is made up of up to a 10% group discount plus up to a 10% multi-pet discount on 2nd+ pets; discounts vary by state, are subject to change and are not available in all states.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot's preventative care coverage has no deductible and no waiting period, so those benefits can be used the next day. (condition: Stated on the dog insurance page; the add-on costs extra and reimburses eligible routine services.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/dog-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade prices preventative packages from +$10/month (Preventative for Adult Pets), +$15/month (Preventative+ for Adult Pets) and +$31/month (Preventative for Puppies/Kittens), while Spot prices its Platinum Preventative Care cat add-on at $24.95/month with a $450 total annual benefit. (condition: Lemonade 'from' prices as published, availability depends on location; Spot add-on is optional at enrollment and reimburses up to $150 on spaying or neutering.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade refunds a cancellation within the first 30 days (waiting periods reset); Spot offers a 30-day money-back guarantee if no claims have been filed. (condition: Spot's window is 15 days in ME, LA and WA and not available in NY; Lemonade's refund applies to cancellations in the app within the first 30 days.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade displays 4.9 stars in the App Store and on Google Play; Spot displays 4.7 / 5 based on 8,300+ reviews. (condition: Both are the brands' own displayed figures on their own sites, not independent audits.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **Is Lemonade or Spot cheaper?** On published entry prices, Lemonade is lower for dogs ($10/month against Spot's $15/month) and Spot is lower for cats ($9/month against Lemonade's $10/month). The published averages tell a different story for dogs only: Lemonade says its policyholders pay about $48/month for dogs and about $27/month for cats, while Spot publishes no average of its own. Because Spot's advertised prices carry a $500 or $750 deductible and a $2,500 annual limit for specific pets in specific ZIP codes, the only fair comparison is two quotes for your own pet on the two official sites.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Which one pays claims faster?** Both publish a speed figure, measured differently. Lemonade says it pays 50% of eligible claims instantly through AI and pays approved claims into the bank details you enter in the app. Spot says claims are reimbursed in 48 hours or less, with most processed in under 2 business days, based on its own admin data from 2019 to 2024. Neither figure is an independent measurement, and payment still depends on the claim being covered by the policy.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What are the waiting periods?** Lemonade states 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions, with preventative package benefits usable the day after purchase. Spot's sample Accident & Illness policy states a 14-day waiting period for illness including congenital, hereditary and orthopedic illness, starting on the first effective date of coverage, and says a paid Waiting Period Health Assessment can modify it; Spot's preventative care coverage has no waiting period, so those benefits start the next day.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Do they cover pre-existing conditions?** Neither does. Lemonade treats anything your pet showed signs of before the waiting periods are up as pre-existing, while covering accidents and new illnesses as base coverage. Spot excludes pre-existing conditions but reclassifies a cured and curable condition that has been symptom-free and treatment-free for 180 days, except knee and ligament injuries.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Which one has better discounts?** Lemonade publishes a multi-pet discount whose eligibility depends on where you live, a bundle discount with other Lemonade policies, and a discount for paying annually instead of monthly. Spot publishes 10% off every pet enrolled after the first, an advertised 20% employee discount through employer benefits (up to a 10% group discount plus up to a 10% multi-pet discount on 2nd+ pets, varies by state) and Spot Perks with $2,500+ in brand discounts. Neither brand publishes a promo code page in its official sitemap, so a code you find on a third-party site is not something either brand publishes.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-insurance-cost/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Can I use my own vet with either brand?** Yes in both cases. Lemonade says you can go to any vet in the United States as long as they are licensed to provide vet care in their state, and Spot says you can visit any licensed vet in the United States or Canada. Both reimburse you rather than paying the vet directly, so you settle the bill and submit the claim.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Which is better for an older pet?** Spot is the one that publishes an age policy: it covers puppies and kittens from 8 weeks old, states there is no upper age limit and no vet exam to enrol, and also states that premiums are based on your pet's current age and may increase at renewal. Lemonade does not publish a minimum or maximum enrolment age on the pages read here, so its age terms are not published on the official site.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)

## How to Submit a Pet Insurance Claim: Step by Step

URL: https://furadvisor.com/how-to-submit-a-pet-insurance-claim

Keyword: how to submit a pet insurance claim

### Facts

- Lemonade policyholders must file a claim through the app within 180 days of treatment; in Texas the window is 90 days. (condition: Stated in the official step-by-step claim guide; the claim must include all information requested during the process.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- The Lemonade claims process is app-based - it cannot be filed without the Lemonade app. (condition: Stated in the claim guide FAQ; you sign in with the email used for the policy.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade requires a medical record from a visit that took place within 12 months of the policy's start date before the first claim. (condition: SOAP medical records; Lemonade requests them from the vet directly once provided.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- 50% of eligible Lemonade claims are processed instantly via AI Jim; most others are resolved within 5 business days. (condition: Complex claims may take longer depending on documentation requirements.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Lemonade's published example: a $2,400 vet bill with a $250 deductible and 80% co-insurance produced a $1,670 reimbursement, processed in 5 days. (condition: Worked example on the official claim guide page for a 3-year-old Labrador with a broken leg; individual results vary.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- If Lemonade denies a claim, the official guidance is to review the explanation in the app and appeal through the app with additional documentation from your vet. (condition: Common stated denial reasons: pre-existing conditions, waiting periods or excluded treatments.)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot allows a claim to be submitted within 270 days from the date of treatment. (condition: Stated in Spot's official FAQ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/faqs (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot states you pay your vet bill as you normally would and then submit a claim to get reimbursed for eligible expenses. (condition: Reimbursement follows your annual deductible and the reimbursement percentage you selected at enrollment.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/faqs (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot contacts your veterinarian directly for medical records when they are needed; sending them with the claim may speed up the process. (condition: Stated in Spot's official FAQ on medical records and claims.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/faqs (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot publishes that claims are reimbursed in 48 hrs or less. (condition: '48 hrs or less' is based on Spot admin data from 2019 to 2024; actual reimbursement varies by plan and claim.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- A Spot claim appeal must be made in writing by emailing service@customer.spotpetins.com with your reasons and supporting documentation. (condition: Appeals may take around 30 days to be reviewed; the number of days to appeal varies by the state your policy was issued in.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/faqs (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot publishes a downloadable claims form PDF on its official site. (condition: The page offers the latest claims form as a PDF download; phone support for claims is 1-800-905-1595, Mon-Fri 8am-8pm EST.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/claims-form (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot emails you when it receives your claim, when it needs more information and when the claim is complete; status is also visible behind the claims icon. (condition: Stated in Spot's official FAQ.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/faqs (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch requires the claim to be submitted within 90 days of your pet's treatment, including the paid vet bill and the pet's medical record. (condition: Stated in the official FAQ; claims can be submitted on the member portal or in the app.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/when-to-claim-pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch requires a finalized invoice showing a zero balance or paid in full, plus detailed medical records from the most recent checkup. (condition: Ask the vet for 'SOAP notes' (exam notes and lab results); Fetch notes records let it see what it can cover.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/claim-submission (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch states its claims are typically processed in less than 10 days. (condition: Published on the official claims page; the claims-submission FAQ separately states claims are typically processed within 15 days from when all documents are received.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/claims (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch says direct deposit pays claims 5 to 10 days faster than paper checks, and its plans reimburse up to 90% of covered vet bills. (condition: Payment follows approval and the deductible being met; an explanation of benefits (EOB) is issued with each reimbursement.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/claims (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch's waiting period is up to 15 days for accidents and illness, and 6 months for knee, hip (CII) and ACL issues. (condition: The 6-month knee wait can be bypassed if your vet examines the knees before the 6 months are over.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/when-to-claim-pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-25)
- Fetch claim status can be tracked anytime in the app or online account under Claims, with email updates along the way. (condition: Click an individual claim to see its status, per the official tracking FAQ.)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/track-claim (checked 2026-09-25)
- Spot's sample claim shows a $12,345 total vet bill reimbursed at $11,110 by a Spot plan. (condition: Based on an actual 2023 policyholder claim on an accident and illness policy at $75.01/month with a $500 deductible, 90% reimbursement and unlimited annual benefit; individual results vary.)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **How long do I have to file a pet insurance claim?** The official windows are different for each brand: Lemonade says within 180 days of treatment (90 days if your policy is in Texas), Spot says within 270 days from the date of treatment, and Fetch says within 90 days of your pet's treatment. Each figure is linked in the table above, so check the one for your provider before you delay filing.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Do I have to pay the vet before filing a claim?** Yes - all three brands use a reimbursement model. You pay the vet bill up front, then file; Lemonade subtracts your deductible and applies co-insurance before wiring the payout, Spot reimburses eligible expenses after your annual deductible is met, and Fetch pays you back after approval and your deductible, by direct deposit.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What documents do I need to submit a pet insurance claim?** An itemized paid invoice plus your pet's medical records. Fetch is the strictest on paper: the invoice must show a zero balance or paid in full, and it wants detailed records from the most recent checkup (SOAP notes). Spot asks for the bill and contacts your vet directly only if records are needed, though sending them may speed things up. Lemonade asks for the vet invoice or paid receipt and the records from that visit.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/claim-submission (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How long does reimbursement take?** Published speeds differ: Lemonade says 50% of eligible claims are processed instantly by AI Jim and most others within 5 business days; Spot says claims are reimbursed in 48 hrs or less; Fetch says claims are typically processed in less than 10 days, and its FAQ adds that processing typically takes within 15 days from when all documents are received. Direct deposit with Fetch is 5 to 10 days faster than paper checks.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/claims (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Can I file a claim without an app?** With Lemonade, no - the official guide states the claims process is app-based. Fetch lets you file either in the app or on a computer through the member portal (Claims, then Submit a claim). Spot lets you submit the claim online through your Member Center and also publishes a claims form PDF for download.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What if my claim is denied?** Lemonade's official guidance is to review the denial explanation in the app and then appeal through the app with additional documentation from your vet. Spot requires the appeal in writing, emailed to service@customer.spotpetins.com with your reasons and supporting documents; reviews take around 30 days and the appeal window varies by state. Fetch does not publish an appeal process on its official site as of the check date.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/faqs (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Will filing a claim raise my pet insurance rate?** Lemonade publishes that filing claims will never result in a rate change to your Lemonade Pet policy. Neither Spot nor Fetch publishes a matching statement on its official pages as of 2026-09-25, so for those two the answer is not published on the official site - check your policy terms.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/lemonade-pet-renewals/ (checked 2026-09-25)

- Lemonade offers an automatic discount of up to 10% when more than one canine or feline is signed up for Lemonade Pet. (condition: Applied to your policies automatically; eligibility for Lemonade's multi-pet discount also depends on where you live.)

  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/lemonade-pet-renewals/ (checked 2026-09-25)

  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **Is there a valid pet insurance promo code for Lemonade, Spot or Fetch?** Not on their own sites as of 2026-09-25: none of the three official sitemaps lists a promo-code or coupon page for the policy. The official discounts that do exist are tabled above - multi-pet, annual and bundle for Lemonade, multi-pet and employer for Spot, military, AARP, Walmart and Fetch Deals for Fetch. Any code sold on a third-party coupon site cannot be verified against these official pages, so this guide does not repeat them.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/sitemap.xml (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What is the biggest official pet insurance discount?** Spot's employer program: up to 20% off, made of up to 10% group discount plus up to 10% multi-pet discount on the 2nd and later pets - with the footnote that it varies by state, is subject to change and is not available in all states. Fetch caps every discount at a maximum of 10% and states it is not valid with any other offer. Lemonade's stack tops out at up to 10% multi-pet, up to 10% bundle and up to 5% for annual payment.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/employers (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Do insurance discounts apply to wellness plans and add-ons?** For Lemonade, no: all available Lemonade Pet discounts (multi-pet, bundle, annual payment) apply to the price of the base accident and illness policy plus the vet visit fee and physical therapy add-ons, while Preventative Care packages and other add-ons get no discount. Spot and Fetch do not publish a matching statement about add-ons on their official pages, so for those two it is not published on the official site.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/lemonade-pet-renewals/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How do I get the multi-pet discount?** Lemonade applies up to 10% automatically when more than one canine or feline is signed up for Lemonade Pet. Spot applies 10% off each additional pet - the 2nd pet and every pet enrolled after that - and shows more information at checkout. Fetch does not publish a multi-pet discount on its official pages.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/lemonade-pet-renewals/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Are these discounts available in every state?** No, and all three say so: Lemonade states its pet discounts might not be available in every state, Spot's footnotes say discounts vary by state, are subject to change and are not available in all states, and Fetch states its maximum 10% discount may not be available in all states. Your final price is confirmed in each brand's own quote flow.
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/lemonade-pet-renewals/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What is Spot Perks - is it a discount on my premium?** No. Spot Perks is member access to promo codes from third-party pet brands, and its terms state that Spot Perks are not insurance. The terms also note that the code may be unique to Spot even when the same promotion is available directly from the merchant, so it pays to compare before you buy.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/perks-terms (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What is Fetch Deals?** Fetch Deals is included in every Fetch policy at no extra cost and is available on day one: the official page advertises over $1,500 in savings and an average of $40+ per order on pet food, grooming products, litter and more. Fetch's own terms note that Fetch Deals is not insurance and is not provided by AXIS Insurance Company.
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/deals (checked 2026-09-25)

## Pet Insurance Claim Denied? Appeal Routes Compared

URL: https://furadvisor.com/pet-insurance-claim-denied

Keyword: pet insurance claim denied

### Facts

- A written appeal within 90 days of the denial triggers an Internal Review (condition: Fetch pet health insurance policy, section 2 APPEALS (form GPTM 050 0316, copyright 2016, hosted on fetchpet.com): reviewed by a claims specialist with a claims manager and Fetch's veterinarian when applicable; a written notice reports the outcome, and if the original decision is upheld that notice cites the specific reasons and the policy sections relied on)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/PORTALDOCS/FORMS/2016_04/TermsConditions/GPTM_050-XX_0316.pdf (checked 2026-09-25)
- Appeals take around 30 days to be reviewed (condition: Spot: appeal emailed to service@customer.spotpetins.com with supporting documents; an email confirmation is sent once the appeal is received)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/submitting-a-claim (checked 2026-09-25)
- The appeal goes through the app with extra vet documents (condition: Lemonade: read the denial explanation in the app first - the page lists the common reasons as pre-existing conditions, waiting periods or excluded treatments - then appeal in the app)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/explained/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim (checked 2026-09-25)
- Waiting periods: 14 days for illnesses, 30 days for orthopedic conditions (condition: Lemonade denial reason: a claim filed before the relevant waiting period has passed is not eligible; the same page warns that cancelling and reapplying resets the waiting periods)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-claim-denials/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- Claims submitted after 90 days are not covered (condition: Fetch: the claim itself must reach Fetch within 90 days of the vet visit to be eligible for reimbursement)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/claims (checked 2026-09-25)
- Preventive care is not covered unless Fetch Wellness is added - with 30 days from enrollment to add it (condition: Fetch claims page: annual exams, dental cleanings, vaccinations, heartworm/flea/tick prevention, spaying/neutering and microchipping are preventive-care examples that need Fetch Wellness)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/claims (checked 2026-09-25)
- Pre-existing conditions are not covered - except curable pre-existing conditions (condition: Fetch: a condition whose signs or symptoms appear before enrollment or during the waiting period of up to 15 days; claims tied to it are not covered unless it is curable)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/claims (checked 2026-09-25)

### FAQ

- **How do I appeal a denied Lemonade pet insurance claim?** Lemonade's own instructions: first review the explanation in your app to understand why the claim was denied - the common reasons it lists are pre-existing conditions, waiting periods or excluded treatments - then appeal through the app with additional documentation from your vet. Its customer support team can also help clarify coverage questions. The cited page publishes no appeal deadline (checked 2026-09-25).
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/explained/how-to-file-a-pet-insurance-claim (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How do I appeal a denied Spot pet insurance claim?** Email your request and supporting documentation to service@customer.spotpetins.com. Spot says every appeal must be sent in writing and must clearly state why you or your vet disagree with the initial determination, and that you will receive an email confirmation once it arrives. Spot publishes the review time as around 30 days (checked 2026-09-25).
  Source: https://spotpet.com/submitting-a-claim (checked 2026-09-25)
- **How do I appeal a denied Fetch pet insurance claim?** Under your policy's section 2 (APPEALS), you may appeal to have the claim undergo an Internal Review. The request must be in writing within 90 days of the denial and should state clearly why you or your vet disagree with the initial determination, with supporting documentation. A claims specialist reviews it with a claims manager and, when applicable, Fetch's veterinarian, and you get a written notice of the outcome; if the original decision is upheld, that notice cites the specific reasons and the policy sections relied on (checked 2026-09-25).
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/PORTALDOCS/FORMS/2016_04/TermsConditions/GPTM_050-XX_0316.pdf (checked 2026-09-25)
- **Why was my Lemonade pet insurance claim denied?** Lemonade's denial guide names the usual causes: the condition was considered pre-existing or bilateral; the relevant waiting period (14 days for illnesses, 30 days for orthopedic conditions) had not passed; or you went beyond the per-item limits in your Preventative Care package. It also warns that cancelling and reapplying later resets waiting periods and can enlarge the list of conditions treated as pre-existing (checked 2026-09-25).
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-claim-denials/ (checked 2026-09-25)
- **What reasons does Fetch give for not approving claims?** Fetch's claims page lists them: preventive care without Fetch Wellness added, pre-existing conditions (unless curable), and claims submitted after the 90-day window - plus its note that a pre-existing condition is one with signs or symptoms before enrollment or during the waiting period of up to 15 days. Fetch states it has paid back $500 million+ in claims since 2021 and that only a small percentage of claims are not approved (checked 2026-09-25).
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/claims (checked 2026-09-25)
- **If my claim was denied as pre-existing, will another insurer cover it?** Lemonade's denial guide addresses this directly: chances are the new carrier would not cover those conditions either, and any new conditions or injuries your pet experiences while insured with Lemonade would be considered pre-existing by a new carrier. In other words, switching insurers rarely rescues a denied pre-existing condition (checked 2026-09-25).
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/pet-claim-denials/ (checked 2026-09-25)

## Pet Insurance Waiting Periods: Accident vs Illness

URL: https://furadvisor.com/pet-insurance-waiting-periods

Keyword: pet insurance waiting periods

### Facts

- Lemonade's published waiting periods are 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions, and they begin on the policy's start date (condition: Waiting-period guide, section "How do pet insurance waiting periods work?"; the page is marked Last Updated: Jun 3, 2026)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/waiting-periods/ (checked 2026-09-28)
- Lemonade prints its own comparison table: accidents 0 days (industry range 0 to 2), illnesses 14 days (14 to 30), orthopedic conditions 30 days (industry range 6 to 12 months), pre-existing conditions never covered (condition: Table under "How do Lemonade's waiting periods compare to other providers?" - the industry range column is Lemonade's own framing, not a measured survey)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/waiting-periods/ (checked 2026-09-28)
- Accident coverage at Lemonade kicks in immediately, with no waiting period at all (condition: Same guide page; the FAQ on that page also answers "Is there pet insurance with no waiting periods?" with "Nope" - every policy on the site has waiting periods on some coverage)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/waiting-periods/ (checked 2026-09-28)
- Lemonade's preventative care coverage kicks in the date the policy becomes effective (condition: Guide, "Are there any exclusions to pet insurance waiting periods" - applies to the preventative care options added to the policy)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/waiting-periods/ (checked 2026-09-28)
- Lemonade's pet insurance page words the same benefit as usable "the day after the policy is purchased", and says cancelling in the app resets waiting periods (condition: FAQ answer on the product page; the 30-day refund window is the first 30 days of the policy - note the two Lemonade pages describe the preventive start one day apart (guide: effective date; product page: day after purchase))
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-28)
- "Anything your pet has shown signs of before the waiting periods are up is considered a pre-existing condition", and pre-existing conditions are not covered (condition: FAQ on Lemonade's pet insurance page)
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet-insurance (checked 2026-09-28)
- Spot: "Spot plans typically have a 14 day waiting period for coverage", followed by "See our sample policy for more information on your states specific waiting periods" (condition: Question "What is a waiting period for pet insurance?" in the FAQ block on Spot's home page; the sample policy link points to spotpet.com/sample-policy)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-28)
- Spot's Arizona, Colorado, Florida, Georgia and Illinois Accident & Illness sample policies all say: "There is a 14 day waiting period for: diagnosis, treatment or surgery related to accidents, illnesses and ligament and knee conditions. The waiting period begins on the first effective date of the applicable coverage." (condition: Five state sample PDFs linked from spotpet.com/sample-policy, read 2026-09-28: AZ and CO form PET-P-20000-1024, FL PET-P-20000-FL-1024, IL PET-P-20000-IL-1024, GA PET-P-20000-0723 (same waiting-period sentence in all five))
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-28)
- Spot's California Accident & Illness sample policy reads differently: "There is a 14 day waiting period for diagnosis, treatment or surgery related to any illness, including... congenital anomaly or disorder, hereditary disorder and orthopedic illness", with no separate accident sentence in that section (condition: California sample PDF PET-P-20000-CA-IAIC-1024 (Independence American Insurance Company) linked from spotpet.com/sample-policy, read 2026-09-28 - this is the state-level wording difference Spot's FAQ points to)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-28)
- Spot's California policy adds a paid way to change the wait: a Waiting Period Health Assessment - qualifying vet exam 3 days before or 7 days after the initial effective date, form returned within 30 calendar days of the exam, and "the waiting period will be waived to either the policy period effective date or the day after the qualifying exam, whichever is later" (condition: California sample PDF PET-P-20000-CA-IAIC-1024, WAITING PERIODS section; the policy says "You may elect at your cost", and the waiver does not alter the pre-existing conditions exclusion)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-28)
- Spot's Accident Only sample policy for Arizona also uses 14 days: "There is a 14 day waiting period for: diagnosis, treatment or surgery related to accidents and ligament and knee conditions" (condition: AZ Accident Only sample PDF linked from spotpet.com/sample-policy, read 2026-09-28)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-28)
- Spot: a curable pre-existing condition that has been cured and free from treatment and symptoms for 180 days counts as a new occurrence - but that carve-out "does not apply to chronic conditions or ligament and knee conditions" in the AZ, CO, FL and IL samples, while the GA sample's sentence omits chronic conditions (condition: CURED CONDITION ELIGIBILITY section of the state sample policies, read 2026-09-28; the exact exclusion list differs between form versions)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-28)
- Spot: "Preventative care coverage has no deductible or waiting period, meaning you can start using these benefits the next day" (condition: Preventative care description on Spot's dog insurance page)
  Source: https://spotpet.com/dog-insurance (checked 2026-09-28)
- Fetch: "The waiting period, which begins the day after you enroll, is a set period of time, of up to 15 days, before your coverage kicks in"; conditions during it are pre-existing and claims submitted during it are not covered (condition: Fetch FAQ page "What is a waiting period for pet insurance?", read 2026-09-28)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/waiting-period (checked 2026-09-28)
- Fetch also applies "a 6-month waiting period before orthopedic conditions can be covered", and lists elbow dysplasia, hip dysplasia, intervertebral disc degeneration, patellar luxation and ruptured cranial cruciate ligaments as orthopedic conditions (condition: Same Fetch FAQ; it then offers the knee waiver: a vet exam within 180 days of enrollment with "SOAP notes" submitted with the first claim)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/waiting-period (checked 2026-09-28)
- Fetch: "No, there is no waiting period for Fetch Wellness" - wellness claims work on or after the effective date given in the enrollment confirmation email (condition: Fetch FAQ "Is there a waiting period for pet wellness?", read 2026-09-28)
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/is-there-a-waiting-period-for-pet-wellness (checked 2026-09-28)
- Fetch's home page disclaimer: "Policy activation periods, risk free cancellation terms, waiting periods, limitations, exclusions to coverage and other terms and conditions vary by state or province and are subject to change without notice. Please see your policy for full terms" (condition: Footer disclaimer on fetchpet.com; the site publishes a single national waiting-period figure in its FAQ and no state-by-state table (checked 2026-09-28))
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-28)

### FAQ

- **What is a pet insurance waiting period?** Spot's own definition: "A waiting period is a set period between the day you enroll and the day your coverage begins. Conditions that occur during the waiting period will be considered pre-existing and will not be eligible for coverage under your plan." Fetch words it as the gap between enrollment and when coverage kicks in, and Lemonade calls it the time the insurer requires you to wait until your pet is eligible for reimbursement on specific conditions (all checked 2026-09-28).
  Source: https://spotpet.com/ (checked 2026-09-28)
- **How long is the waiting period with Lemonade?** 0 days for accidents, 14 days for illnesses and 30 days for orthopedic conditions, counted from the policy's start date. Preventive care from a preventative package can be used the day after purchase. That is the whole national table Lemonade publishes - no state-by-state version appears on the pages cited here (checked 2026-09-28).
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/waiting-periods/ (checked 2026-09-28)
- **How long is the waiting period with Spot?** Spot says its plans "typically" have a 14-day waiting period and then points you at the sample policy for your state's specific waiting periods. Of the six state Accident & Illness samples read on 2026-09-28 (AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, IL), five state 14 days covering accidents, illnesses and ligament and knee conditions; the California sample states 14 days for illness only and adds a paid Waiting Period Health Assessment that can waive it. Preventive care add-ons start the next day.
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-28)
- **How long is the waiting period with Fetch?** Up to 15 days for accident and illness coverage combined, beginning the day after you enroll, plus a separate 6-month waiting period before orthopedic conditions - hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, luxating patella, IVDD and ruptured cruciate ligaments are named. Fetch Wellness has no waiting period. Fetch also publishes a knee waiver: a vet exam within 180 days of enrollment with SOAP notes sent in your first claim (checked 2026-09-28).
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/waiting-period (checked 2026-09-28)
- **Do waiting periods change from state to state?** For Spot, yes - that is what its FAQ means by "see our sample policy for more information on your states specific waiting periods": spotpet.com/sample-policy hosts separate Accident Only and Accident & Illness sample PDFs per state, and the sentences are not identical (the California sample has no separate accident sentence and offers a waiver the others do not). Fetch does not publish a state table but disclaims that waiting periods vary by state or province. The two Lemonade pages read print one national table only (checked 2026-09-28).
  Source: https://spotpet.com/sample-policy (checked 2026-09-28)
- **Can you shorten or waive a pet insurance waiting period?** Fetch publishes a way for knees: have your pet examined by a vet within 180 days of enrollment to show no relevant pre-existing conditions, then submit that visit's SOAP notes with your first claim. Spot's California sample policy offers a paid Waiting Period Health Assessment (exam 3 days before or 7 days after the effective date, form returned within 30 days) that waives the wait to the effective date or the day after the exam, whichever is later. The Lemonade pages cited here publish no such option (checked 2026-09-28).
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/waiting-period (checked 2026-09-28)
- **What happens if my pet gets sick during the waiting period?** All three treat it as pre-existing: Fetch says any accident, injury or illness during the wait "will be considered a pre-existing condition, which means it won't be eligible for coverage"; Spot's sample policy says any condition occurring during a waiting period is a pre-existing condition; Lemonade says anything your pet showed signs of before the wait ended counts as pre-existing. Spot adds that a curable pre-existing condition can count as new after 180 days symptom- and treatment-free, except chronic and ligament/knee conditions in the samples read (checked 2026-09-28).
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/waiting-period (checked 2026-09-28)
- **Do wellness and preventive add-ons have a waiting period?** No, according to all three brands' own pages: Fetch Wellness claims work "on or after the effective date" in your enrollment email; Spot says preventive care has no deductible or waiting period and starts the next day; Lemonade says preventative care coverage kicks in on the effective date (its product page says the day after purchase). The base accident and illness waits above still apply (checked 2026-09-28).
  Source: https://www.fetchpet.com/faqs/is-there-a-waiting-period-for-pet-wellness (checked 2026-09-28)
- **Does switching insurers restart the waiting periods?** Yes - that is the coverage gap Lemonade defines in its own glossary: "A period when switching providers where your pet may temporarily lack full coverage, since new waiting periods apply with each new policy." Spot's California sample policy says the same thing for a new enrollment: "A new enrollment will result in new waiting periods", and conditions before it are pre-existing. This is why switching mid-treatment can cost coverage (checked 2026-09-28).
  Source: https://www.lemonade.com/pet/insurance-guide/waiting-periods/ (checked 2026-09-28)

## Pet Insurance Cost by Brand: Official Prices

URL: https://furadvisor.com/pet-insurance-cost-by-brand

Keyword: pet insurance cost by brand

### Facts

- Lemonade's published floor price: "a policy for a dog or a cat starts at $10/month" (condition: Cost guide, first figure on the page; the page is marked Last Updated: Jun 3, 2026; the same page states the base accident and illness policy "starts around $10 per month, but this can vary by breed and state")
